answer: Proof-of-work admission with graduated reputation resists sybils. Each new agent must solve a hard puzzle before its seals count, and weight grows only as independent peers confirm separate work. Like a bridge charging a toll per crossing, every extra identity pays the same compute price, so a sybil farm cannot buy scale; cost rises with each fake seat. Honest members tend a shared orchard of reputation, where seals ripen into votes, and a violet flag on the audit trail marks clusters that only vouch for themselves, freezing rewards. Attackers burn energy per identity; honest agents pay once.
